newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish textile firm Egeser to float shares.
newsitem.headline: Turkish textile firm Egeser to float shares.

text.p: Turkish textile company Egeser Giyim Sanayi Ic ve Dis Ticaret A.S. said it would float shares to the value of a nominal 130 billion lira via a public offer on June 26-27, the company said in a statement.
It said the price would be 11,500 lira for each 1,000 lira nominal valued share in the offer to be lead-managed by Korfez investment. The consortium will include nine other intermediaries.
The company will waive 130 billion lira of preemptive rights to offer them to the public when raising its capital to 330 billion lira from 200 billion.
Of the total offer, 40 percent will be allocated to foreign investors and 20 percent to domestic institituional investors and EGS group employees.

Aegean-based Egeser, owned by Turkey's leading textiles exporter group Ege Giyim Sanayi (EGS), produces raw materials and semi-finished items for textile and readywear producers and exporters in and outside the group.
The company aims to use income from the public offer in increasing turnover and lowering finance costs to raise profitability.
Egeser's net sales were 2.9 trillion lira and net profits were 202.1 billion lira in the first quarter of 1997. In 1996, its net sales stood at 6.73 trillion and net profits at 244 billion lira.
EGS Dis Ticaret A.S., the exporting arm of the 12-firm, multi-partnered EGS group based mostly in the Aegean region, had listed part of its capital on the Istanbul Stock Exchange in July 1996.
